captions.instagram:
How does a squid change color?

A squid’s shimmer is not paint. It is light bouncing off stacks of protein plates thinner than a soap film, and a nerve signal can squeeze water out of them to slide the colour from red to blue. Some squid go further and make their own light.

→ A squid is a muscle tube with fins, ten limbs and a funnel that fires a jet.
→ Inside run two giant nerves, half a millimetre thick, that fire the escape jet.
→ Squid skin hides stacks of protein plates thinner than a soap film. They reflect one colour.
→ A nerve signal squeezes water out: the plates thin and the colour slides from red to blue.
→ Seen from below, a bobtail squid would cast a shadow. Glowing bacteria on its belly erase it.

A squid’s shimmer is not paint. It is light bouncing off stacks of protein plates thinner than a soap film, and a nerve signal can squeeze water out of them to slide the colour from red to blue. Some squid go further and make their own light.

In this video:
• A jet-powered tube. A squid is a muscular mantle with fins, eight arms, two tentacles and a funnel that fires a jet.
• Mirrors it can tune. Iridophores hold stacks of reflectin plates about a tenth of a micrometre thick.
• Making light. The Hawaiian bobtail squid farms glowing Vibrio fischeri bacteria in a light organ and matches the moonlight to hide its shadow from below.
• Jet and ink. Squeezing the mantle shoots water from the funnel and the squid goes tail first.
• Squid and people. India landed about 2.13 lakh tonnes of cephalopods in 2023, roughly half squid, mostly the Indian squid.
• How we found out. Aristotle described squid ink.
